scenes.say: Ever wonder why Docker talks about images and containers like they're different things? Let's clear this up for good.

scenes.label: Image
scenes.sub: A read-only template, built in layers.
scenes.say: First, an image is just a template. It's read-only, and built up layer by layer from a Dockerfile.

scenes.label: Container
scenes.sub: A running instance with its own writable layer.
scenes.say: A container is what you get when you run an image. It's a live instance, with its own thin writable layer on top.

rows.b: Only the container can change data

scenes.say: You build an image from a recipe. When you run it, Docker adds a writable layer. That's where your app writes data.
One image can run as many containers as you want. Each gets its own writable space, but shares the same template.

scenes.question: Where does container data live?
scenes.right: In the container's writable layer, which is lost when the container is deleted unless you use a volume.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Data written by your app isn't saved in the image. It's in the container's writable layer, and gone when you remove the container—unless you use a volume.
